title: RentGuard Renters Policy — Start Date of the Days Credited on a Discount Restart
content:
Restart start date. When the multi-policy discount on a RentGuard Renters Policy restarts because a new Larkspur Valuables Floater or Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy took effect, the day from which the days credited for the restart run depends on how far ahead the new qualifying policy was bound and on its own billing plan.

**Clause.** When the new qualifying policy was bound 14 calendar days or more before it took effect and is billed on the annual plan, the days credited for the restart run from its bound date to the renters expiration date; when it was bound 14 calendar days or more before it took effect and is billed on any other plan, the days credited run from 7 calendar days before its effective date to the renters expiration date, and never from a day before the renters effective date; when it was bound fewer than 14 calendar days before it took effect, the days credited run from its effective date.

**Inputs read from the new umbrella or floater record:** bound date, effective date, billing plan. **Input read from the renters policy:** effective date and expiration date of the renters term.

| Calendar days from its bound date to its effective date | Its billing plan | Days credited run from |
|---|---|---|
| 14 or more | Annual plan | Its bound date |
| 14 or more | Two-pay, monthly EFT or monthly card plan | 7 calendar days before its effective date, never earlier than the renters effective date |
| 13 or fewer | Any plan | Its effective date |

### Hypothetical cases

1. Floater bound 1 April, effective 15 April (14 days ahead), annual plan: the days credited run from 1 April.
2. Same floater bound 2 April (13 days ahead): the days credited run from 15 April.
3. Umbrella bound 14 days ahead on a monthly plan, effective 20 May: the days credited run from 13 May.
4. As in case 3, but the renters term began on 16 May: the days credited run from 16 May, never from a day before the renters effective date — the whole renters term at most.
